title: Undo brings the band back without bringing back what it caught
goal: Sweep a band round two things and stack them, then press Undo: the two things come back and the dotted band comes back, but neither of them is picked any more. The inspector goes empty and you have to sweep the band again before you can stack them a second time, even though the band is sitting right there on screen.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-08 on the probe while fixing undo-does-not-take-apart-a-stack-made-from-a-mar.

  Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/stack-from-a-band-walk.json

Stage states out of /tmp/photonz-playtest/stack-from-a-band/log.json:
  [1-band-caught-both] layers: 3  region: 80,50 440x330  sel: [Rectangle, Rectangle 2]
  [2-stacked]          layers: 2  region: none            sel: [Group]
  [3-one-undo]         layers: 3  region: 80,50 440x330  sel: []      <- band back, pick gone
  [4-redone]           layers: 2  region: none            sel: []      <- redo loses it too
See queue/audits/2026-09-08-stack-band-undo-1.png: no row is highlighted in the Layers list.

NOT a regression from that fix; it is general. SelectionSnapshot (PhotonzCore) carries only region + targetsPixels, so which LAYERS were picked has never been part of an undo step. Fixing it means either widening the snapshot or re-deriving the pick from the restored band the way setSelection(captureLayers: true) does. Note the band-caught-nothing case: setSelection keeps that as a pixel region on the layer you had, so a re-derive must not clobber it (SelectionHistoryTests pins the contract).
acceptance: After undoing a stack made from a band, the things the band caught are picked again, so the inspector reads them and Stack Selection is available straight away
Redo leaves the picking right too, not just the drawing
A band that caught nothing stays a pixel region on undo, exactly as it does now
A walk covers undo restoring the pick
